fete.titre: 13 days of festivities in the corsair city
texte: The Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe is also a story of atmosphere that brings together millions of people in the activity villages at the start and finish. A union of enthusiasts, amateurs, or simply curious onlookers, all come to admire these extraordinary men and women.

The Brittany region and the corsair city see their sailors preparing to assault the ocean, while the Guadeloupe region and Pointe-à-Pitre admire the triumph of having succeeded in reaching the other side of the Atlantic!

texte: A historic city in Brittany, built between the 17th and 18th centuries, distinguished by the richness and beauty of its heritage and environment, Saint-Malo has retained all its authenticity.

Always oriented towards the open sea, the city has been the historic starting point of the Route du Rhum – Destination Guadeloupe since its first sailings in 1978, and embodies its love for the sea in all its forms. A land of great navigators, from explorers and discoverers to privateers, Cape Horn captains, fishermen and other renowned offshore racers, the Corsair City has been pursuing an active policy in culture and hosting major sailing events for over four decades.

The Breton port is always delighted to see those passionate about the open sea and freedom flock to its ramparts, giving the walled city and quays a unique and unparalleled atmosphere. It’s a place where popular enthusiasm meets almost intimate reunions with the men and women preparing to embark on the most prestigious of solo ocean races.
ville.chute: Saint-Malo represents 48 years of unconditional attachment to this race and a shared history that will forever leave its mark in its wake.

texte: With the current drought alert in Ille-et-Vilaine, particular attention will be paid to how water is used. Like all users and stakeholders in the area, the Route du Rhum - Destination Guadeloupe is subject to the restrictions in force under the prefectural drought order, and intends to play its full part in the collective effort to use water sparingly, working alongside the City of Saint-Malo and the Brittany Region.

This vigilance will come with a dedicated information and awareness scheme. Participants, exhibitors and caterers will be informed of the restrictions in place and the good practices to follow. The public will also be made aware before and during the event, through the eco-friendly visitor guide, social media and dedicated communication in the Village.

programme.chapo: From Tuesday, October 20th to Sunday, November 1st, 2026, thirteen days of festivities on the quays of Saint-Malo.
